literal: Family lineage will burn if conduct is slipped; goodness will burn if shamelessness abides.
translation: A slip in right conduct will destroy one's lineage; but if shamelessness takes root, it will destroy every good quality one possesses.
modern: ஒருவர் தன் ஒழுக்கத்திலிருந்து தவறினால் அது அவருடைய குலத்தை அழிக்கும்; ஆனால் அவரிடம் வெட்கமின்மை நிலைத்து நின்றால், அது அவருடைய எல்லா நன்மைகளையும் அழித்துவிடும்.
explanation: This couplet contrasts the consequences of failing in one's conduct with the far more devastating consequences of losing one's sense of shame. If a person slips from their principles of conduct, that failure destroys the reputation of their lineage. However, if shamelessness becomes a permanent state in them, it burns away and destroys all their inherent goodness and virtues. The poet uses the metaphor of burning to show how both failures act like a destructive fire, but shamelessness is the ultimate destroyer of a person's entire character.
